Confirmed against the 2026 calendar: Group 1 opened 2026-08-03 and closed 2026-09-01 (a 29-day span), so counting 30 days forward overshoots the real deadline. A user can file on time and still lose on evidence. Source: https://www.cookcountyboardofreview.com/sites/g/files/ywwepo261/files/document/file/2026-08/2026TOWNSHIPOPEN-CLOSE.pdf
dependsOn.filingFee: $0 VERIFIED for the Board of Review only ('At the Board of Review filing is free') at https://www.cookcountyboardofreview.com/about/frequently-asked-questions — the Assessor's Office half of waiverConditions is UNVERIFIED.
dependsOn.levels: VERIFIED that PTAB and Circuit Court are ALTERNATIVES, not sequential steps, per the Board of Review FAQ.
dependsOn.argumentTypes: UNRESOLVED. The Board of Review Official Rules do not enumerate permissible grounds, and the BOR frames its role as appeals of 'over-valuation' — which does not confirm UNIFORMITY as the primary residential ground. primaryArgument selects the entire ratio model in ratio.ts, so this is high-stakes. Re-check https://www.cookcountyboardofreview.com/board-review-official-rules
dependsOn.assessmentLevelPctOfMarket: UNRESOLVED. The Cook County Classification Ordinance could not be reached from any official host (ilga.gov, tax.illinois.gov, illinois.gov, cookcountyassessoril.gov all unreachable). Only secondary summaries support 10%. Do NOT set citations[].verified on this value until the ordinance itself is read.
dependsOn.estimatedTaxRateOnAssessedBps: UNRESOLVED, and it is multiplied directly into the user-facing 'estimated annual overpayment' in verdict.ts. Cook's real burden is assessment level x STATE EQUALIZATION FACTOR x composite local rate; the equalizer is re-struck annually by the Illinois Dept of Revenue. Model the factors explicitly rather than collapsing them into one constant.
dependsOn.compsWindowMonths: UNRESOLVED — no published standard found in any reachable source. Unsourced default.
dependsOn.reliefModel: Added 2026-08-15 as a schema field only, no Cook value changed. GAP means 'no statutory ratio corridor constrains the board', which is the engine's default and matches how Cook outcomes were already being decided. If Illinois turns out to apply a median-level test comparable to New Jersey's Chapter 123, this must be revisited — it was NOT verified, because the Assessor's site is bot-blocked.
